          "text": "# Alpha2 Cru: A blue point at the foot of the Cross\n\n*In the Southern Cross, Acrux offers a bright landmark\u2014and a close pairing to explore with a telescope.*\n\nAs dusk deepens in the Southern Hemisphere\u2019s autumn, the Southern Cross climbs into view. Its brightest star, Acrux, marks the Cross\u2019s southern end. Look closely with a telescope and the single bright point resolves into two stars: Alpha1 Cru and Alpha2 Cru. The second of these, Alpha2 Cru, is a blue-white star with a catalogue identity all its own: HD 108249.\n\nThe distinction is a useful reminder that stars with nearly the same address can be separate objects. SIMBAD identifies HD 108249 as Alpha2 Cru and gives its position as right ascension 12h 26m 36.442s, declination \u221263\u00b0 05\u2032 58.28\u2033 (J2000). The database lists its visual magnitude as 1.58, bright enough to be seen without optical aid under ordinary conditions. It also assigns the star a B1V spectral type: \u201cB\u201d indicates a hot, blue-white star, while \u201cV\u201d denotes a main-sequence star. SIMBAD flags that classification as low quality, so it is best treated as a catalogue description rather than a finely pinned-down measurement.\n\nAlpha2\u2019s brilliance makes it a fine naked-eye guidepost, but its close companion is the real observing invitation.
